transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what finally pushed me to make the appointment is I keep getting up when I really should be staying seated. Like during sprint planning at work, or even on calls with the mortgage people, I’ll suddenly decide I need water or I should check something in the other room.

And it sounds small when I say it, but it’s gotten embarrassing. Like, I know I should just sit there and finish the call, but I’m already halfway up before I’ve really thought it through. Sprint planning is already kind of a whole thing anyway—we use this board that everyone has opinions about—but, yeah, the main thing is I can’t seem to stay put when I’m supposed to.

Thinking back, did you notice this kind of restlessness and difficulty staying seated as a child or teenager, or is this something that's really only become a problem more recently, say in the last several months or years?

Yeah, it definitely goes back. I mean, I didn’t think of it as a “thing” then, but in elementary school I remember teachers moving my desk around or putting me closer to them because I was always popping up out of my seat.

And I’d talk before I was called on, too—like I knew the answer and it would just come out. Or I’d rush through assignments even when I understood them, which is funny because I actually liked school for the most part. I had this one teacher who used to tap my desk with her pencil—sorry, that’s probably not important—but, yeah, it wasn’t just recently. It was there when I was a kid.
Aside from the restlessness, do you also notice trouble staying focused on tasks, following through on details, or often losing track of what you're doing—both now and back when you were a kid?

Yeah, I mean… yes, there is some of that. It’s not always dramatic, but I’ll sit down to review a pull request and I really do mean to focus on it, and then a few minutes later I realize I’m just staring at the same chunk of code and my brain is off thinking about, like, whether I paid the water bill or what we’re doing for dinner.

Same thing with the mortgage documents recently — which, honestly, those are kind of impossible to read anyway — but I’ll start with good intentions and then catch myself rereading the same section over and over because I’ve drifted off into five unrelated thoughts. I guess it happened when I was younger too, but now I notice it more because the stuff I’m supposed to focus on actually matters.
Beyond work, do these patterns of restlessness or losing focus also cause problems for you at home or in your personal relationships?

Yeah, it does. I mean, not in a huge dramatic way, but enough that it’s starting to be… noticeable, I guess.

At home, my partner has to circle back with me on things more than they used to — like plans or little tasks we said we’d handle. And then at work it’s similar, where someone follows up and I’m like, “Right, yes, I meant to do that,” and I hate that feeling. It makes me worry I’m becoming the unreliable one, especially with planning stuff.

Which is frustrating because I really am trying. I’m not just blowing things off. I’ll have every intention of doing the thing, and then somehow it turns into this whole chain of reminders and follow-ups. And then I feel bad because I know everyone’s busy — sorry, I’m rambling — but yes, it’s causing friction both at work and at home.
Have you been experiencing any ongoing feelings of anxiety, worry, or low mood recently that might be contributing to these concentration and restlessness issues?

I don’t know… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed anything like that as the main thing. I get stressed, sure, but who doesn’t? Especially with work deadlines and all the random life admin stuff — I swear there’s always some form or email or something I forgot to answer.

But low mood or ongoing anxiety… I’m not sure. It doesn’t feel like that’s what’s driving it, at least not to me. I can be in a perfectly fine mood and still have the same issue where I’m bouncing around mentally or can’t stay with one thing.

Would you say these attention and restlessness difficulties have been fairly constant throughout your life from childhood into adulthood, or were there stretches—like in high school or early adulthood—where they were much less noticeable or seemed to go away?

I think it’s been there pretty much the whole time, yeah. I mean, it probably looked different depending on the age, but in elementary school I remember teachers moving my desk around or putting me closer to them because I couldn’t stay put.

Like I’d pop up out of my seat, or start talking before they called on me, or I’d rush through assignments even when I actually understood the work. Which is funny because I liked school in some ways — I liked getting new notebooks, and I was weirdly particular about pencils — sorry, that’s not really the point.

But no, I don’t remember it fully going away. It was more like sometimes I could compensate better, or the situation made it less obvious.

Have you ever had distinct periods—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt on top of the world, followed by a return to your usual self?

I’m not sure… I don’t think so? Like, I definitely have days where I’m kind of wired and I take on too much, especially if I get into a project or I’m excited about something. I’ll stay up later than I meant to because I’m fixing some tiny thing in code or reorganizing a closet at the worst possible time — which, now that I say it out loud, sounds ridiculous.

But the “several days” thing, or needing way less sleep and feeling amazing or unstoppable… I don’t know that I’ve noticed that as a pattern. I usually still need sleep, and if I don’t get it, I feel it. I’m not sure if that answers what you mean.
